Theme

Conversation, family & daily routines

you’re right phrase

also well said, good thinking!, good idea!, you’re quite right, you heard right

classical

Traupman 107
Ter. Eun. 3.1.61: Bene dīxtī, “you are right” (Lewis & Short s.v. bene: “a formula of approbation”)

Bene dīxistī.

you’re right, well said

Other words

  • Rēctē putās. — you’re right, good thinking

    also used · classical · Ter. And. 1.1.114 (Lewis & Short), s.v. putō

  • Bene putās. — good thinking!

    also used · modern · Traupman 99; Traupman 322

    Traupman’s phrase; Terence’s rēctē putās is the attested one.

  • Facētē dictum! — well said! good one!

    also used · classical · Plaut. Capt. 1.2.73; Ter. Eun. 2.2.57, 3.1.37 (Lewis & Short s.v. facētus); Traupman 111, 405

    (vōx cōmica: Plaut., Ter.)

    Praise for a witty remark rather than a true one: facētē, wittily.

  • Vēra dīcis. — you’re right, what you say is true

    also used · classical · Plaut. Am. 1.1.239: vēra dīcō (Lewis & Short s.v. vērus); Plaut. Cas. 2.3.18: vēra dīcās velim, I wish you told the truth (Lewis & Short s.v. volō); Traupman 107

    Plautus’ vēra dīcere, to tell the truth; the second person is Traupman’s, built the same way.

Examples

  • «Nōn attulit! Mīnōtaurus Conimbrigae manet!» «Bene dīxistī.»

    “He didn’t bring it! The Minotaur stays at Conimbriga!” “You’re right.”Libellus III, Apud avum et aviam

  • Vēra dīcis.

    You’re right (what you say is true).Traupman 107, 132

  • Rēctē audīvistī.

    You heard right.Traupman 146

See also that’s right.

SourcesJohn C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 99, 107, 111, 322.
